articles.summary: L'Appel de Paris pour la sécurité de l'IA, publié par l'Élysée le 9 novembre 2026, réunissait le 18 novembre 18 États, 10 entreprises et 11 organisations. Les développeurs s'y engagent à des mécanismes d'arrêt de leurs modèles, entraînement et usage interne compris, mais seulement pour les modèles qu'ils contrôlent : les copies de modèles à poids ouverts y échappent, et aucune autorité ne peut ordonner un arrêt. Le texte ne prévoit ni sanction ni échéance. Google, Meta et xAI, signataires le 29 septembre d'un accord de la Maison-Blanche sans clause d'arrêt, sont absents, comme les États-Unis e
articles.excerpt: L'engagement le plus concret de l'Appel de Paris, pouvoir arrêter un modèle d'IA, ne vise que les modèles que leurs développeurs ont déjà le pouvoir d'arrêter. Dans ce texte publié par l'Élysée le 9 novembre 2026, après une session de travail en visioconférence d'une cinquantaine de participants, les développeurs s'engagent à des mécanismes capables d'interrompre « le fonctionnement des modèles placés sous leur contrôle » . Ce qui tourne ailleurs n'est pas concerné. Et personne d'autre qu'eux ne décide. Le 18 novembre, la liste de l'Élysée comptait 18 États, 10 entreprises et 11 organisations de la société civile. Elle s'est allongée depuis le 9 novembre, quand la déclaration du gouvernement canadien ne recensait que six pays ; l'Allemagne, puis l'Espagne, font partie des nouveaux venus. Les entreprises sont Anthropic, Black Forest Labs, Cohere, Domyn, Hugging Face, Microsoft, Mistral AI, OpenAI, Sakana AI et Synthesia. Parmi les organisations figurent LawZero, fondée par Yoshua Bengio, l'Ifri et le CeSIA. Trois engagements composent le texte. Le premier promet un cadre commun pour évaluer les modèles de frontière, les systèmes les plus avancés, face aux usages malveillants, du piratage aux armes chimiques, et au risque de perte de contrôle, avec la publication des résultats non sensibles dans un format standardisé. L'alerte sur les incidents graves relève du troisième. Le deuxième, consacré à la responsabilité, porte la clause d'arrêt : restreindre, mettre en pause ou couper un modèle, y compris pendant l'entraînement et l'usage interne. Viser l'entraînement et l'usage interne n'a rien d'anodin. articles.title: Nvidia relève sa prévision et écarte le retour de Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia publie 115,8 milliards de dollars de chiffre d'affaires pour le trimestre clos le 25 octobre, au-dessus de sa prévision, et vise 130 milliards pour le suivant, qui compte quatorze semaines. Colette Kress, directrice générale par intérim, relève à environ 75 % la croissance attendue sur l'exercice 2028. Le conseil a accepté la démission de Jensen Huang, n'entend pas le rétablir et crée un comité de surveillance des exportations. Les ventes sous licence en Chine ont cessé et la prévision n'en tient plus compte.
articles.excerpt: Avant le premier chiffre, la conférence de résultats de Nvidia a donné la parole, le 17 novembre, au président de son conseil d'administration, une fonction que le groupe n'avait pas une semaine plus tôt. Harvey Jones a déclaré que le conseil, unanime, avait accepté la démission de Jensen Huang, qu'il n'entendait pas le rétablir à la direction générale et qu'aucune question ne serait prise sur les circonstances de son départ. Colette Kress, directrice financière et directrice générale par intérim, a ensuite annoncé 115,8 milliards de dollars de chiffre d'affaires pour le trimestre clos le 25 octobre, prévu 130 milliards pour le suivant et relevé à environ 75 % la croissance attendue sur l'exercice 2028, contre 70 % en août. Pendant les questions des analystes, Colette Kress a affirmé que « la demande dépasse de loin l'offre ». En août, ce discours revenait à Jensen Huang, qui assurait que la demande était « bien supérieure à 70 % » quand la directrice financière s'en tenait à la prévision chiffrée. Elle tient désormais les deux rôles. L'offre reste le facteur limitant pour les clients. En août, Colette Kress prévoyait que cette tension durerait au moins jusqu'à la fin de l'exercice 2028, en janvier 2028. Nvidia dit avoir sécurisé la mémoire et l'encapsulation avancée dont dépendent ses livraisons. Le communiqué publié le 17 novembre dépasse la fourchette que Nvidia s'était fixée le 26 août, 108 milliards de dollars à 2 % près, soit 110,2 milliards au plus. articles.summary: H Company rend sa plateforme d'agents d'IA disponible sur l'AWS European Sovereign Cloud. L'inférence des clients européens qui le demandent tourne dans l'Union, sur des instances gérées par Nvidia ; l'entraînement des modèles reste sur l'infrastructure mondiale d'AWS. Les contenus et métadonnées des clients restent dans l'UE. Une entreprise européenne de services financiers, non nommée, sera la première utilisatrice.
articles.excerpt: H Company, la société parisienne spécialisée dans les agents d'IA pour les entreprises, a annoncé le 16 novembre que sa plateforme est disponible sur l'AWS European Sovereign Cloud. Les organisations européennes des secteurs réglementés et du secteur public peuvent ainsi, dès maintenant, faire travailler ses agents sur une infrastructure où leurs données et leurs métadonnées ne quittent pas l'Union européenne. Le partage est net. H Company exécute sur le cloud souverain d'AWS l'inférence des clients européens qui le demandent, sur des instances gérées par Nvidia. L'entraînement de ses modèles, lui, reste sur l'infrastructure mondiale d'AWS. Ce qui reste dans l'Union, ce sont les contenus des clients et les métadonnées qu'ils créent, autrement dit tout ce que les agents voient et produisent quand ils travaillent. Pour ce type d'agents, la localisation compte. Ceux de H Company utilisent les logiciels comme le ferait un salarié : ils cliquent, saisissent du texte, naviguent d'un écran à l'autre, et opèrent directement sur les systèmes existants, sans intégration d'API ni modification des applications. Ils traitent donc en temps réel les données opérationnelles de l'organisation, celles qui s'affichent à l'écran d'un conseiller bancaire ou d'un gestionnaire de dossiers. articles.summary: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.
articles.excerpt: Nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday , up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies. The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it shows how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year ; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year. But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor. Nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.” Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic, OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications. It’s also become a big financier of the data center build out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio. articles.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
articles.summary: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now live inside Copilot; always-on agents are next.
articles.excerpt: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now live inside Copilot; always-on agents are next. Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.” The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them. Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. articles.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
articles.summary: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.
articles.excerpt: Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang , the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop. On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations. “We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.” The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases. Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading. Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership ⁠ (opens in a new window) today to help more people discover and engage with Le Figaro’s journalism. The partnership covers current reporting and archive content from Le Figaro and associated publications, spanning news, business, culture and lifestyle. These articles will be discoverable using summaries and excerpts, including links to underlying stories. Le Figaro will retain full editorial independence and control over its journalism. The partnership builds on OpenAI’s work with news organisations around the world to improve the discovery of reliable information, create responsible applications of AI for publishers, and develop new ways for audiences to engage with original reporting. Le Figaro also plans to introduce ChatGPT Enterprise across various teams to support their day-to-day work. It will explore additional uses of OpenAI technology in its workflows and reader services, guided by its AI charter and editorial standards.

articles.excerpt: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country. China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies , export control compliance, and global trade risks. Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff. The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.” Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely. Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue. The platform, which serves more than 18 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the company’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.” So far, Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call. “Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” said Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face. articles.excerpt: External sandboxes for coding agents . I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant , the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects . My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox. To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations: Each of these implementations offers the same localhost API. You can then configure Pi, Claude Code, or Codex to send API calls to that sandbox any time they want to execute code. The sandboxes also include an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code is allowed to communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent. Here's the UI you can use to reconfigure that proxy while the sandbox is still running: I continue to be fascinated by the challenge of safely running untrusted code. articles.excerpt: Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google. While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact). Even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the company. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the days when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity. These notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing says.) But it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise). Google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. articles.excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Commission is opening a civil probe into Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, according to The Wall Street Journal . The investigation adds to Nvidia’s stack of drama after CEO Jensen Huang resigned following news of his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed. The Commerce Department has been investigating Megaspeed since late 2024 under suspicion that the company diverted some of its Nvidia chips to China, which would violate U.S. export laws. Congress has also demanded that Huang answer questions about his affair and how it might have affected his stance that export restrictions should be loosened. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put it more bluntly over the weekend, accusing Nvidia of knowingly selling powerful chips to China to “goose their revenues and their earnings.” The news of the SEC probe also comes as Nvidia reports earnings to a market that has seen its stock fall more than 10% since Huang departed. The chipmaker reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago. articles.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it’s not having one
articles.summary: With tech outages seemingly everywhere, Google took the unusual step of announcing that Gmail is working just fine, actually.
articles.excerpt: Was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company said it was not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded users they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard . As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own . While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others said they were not having any problems. The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users. The fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. Over the past week, Apple and Microsoft experienced outages, an FAA network failure led to a nationwide ground stop, and some banks and airlines also reported disruptions. However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox Business Network’s “The Claman Countdown” on Tuesday that the U.S. is not currently facing coordinated cyberattacks. articles.excerpt: Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors. Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022. Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis. Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April. Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results. The change , which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12. OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations. Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models. The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models. Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. articles.summary: Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities.
articles.excerpt: In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier. Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model. TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week). However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately. The action is happening on both ends of the ecosystem: Sqwish , a U.K.-based AI startup behind a decision model called kettei fat, announced a $3 million pre-seed round today. Co-founders Ushnish Sengupta and Federica Freddi, who met as Cambridge grad students, had been developing small LLMs when Jev arrived on the scene, and they realized their architectures could be repurposed as a powerful decision model. articles.summary: Proton's new Lumo Desktop app for Windows, Mac, and Linux lets users automate tasks across files and connected apps, with granular controls over what its AI can access.
articles.excerpt: Proton , the privacy-focused tech company offering alternatives to Google’s and Microsoft’s tools for email, productivity apps, password management, cloud storage, and more, is now bringing its AI app Lumo to personal computers. On Tuesday, the company launched Lumo Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux, allowing users to leverage its AI to carry out local tasks on their computer involving connected apps, personal files, and other automations. The app is designed to offer users more control over their personal data, as consumer AI technology becomes focused more on AI agents that can perform tasks on users’ behalf, rather than just answering questions. Already, the major model makers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others, offer desktop tools for working with their AI technologies, but doing so invites increased risk to users’ personal data . Only this week, for instance, Apple announced it was addressing those privacy concerns with tightened security settings for apps that request Full Disk Access, as the AI desktop apps do. Proton’s idea is to offer a set of tools that let its AI access connected apps, files, and folders and automate tasks, but with more personalization over how much access the AI has. The company says users can choose which actions the AI agent takes that will need to request their approval, and it vows that the conversations and information from connected apps and files are never used to serve personalized ads or train AI models. The new app includes a variety of connectors that support local tools, like file-system access, shell execution, and browser content fetching, as well as Proton’s email app and other third-party services, including Confluence, Dropbox, and Jira. articles.title: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it’s a game
articles.summary: Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. They usually compiled.
articles.excerpt: Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals. Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery. The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game. The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence. Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency it could not use Anthropic’s technology for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has insisted that today’s AI systems aren’t reliable enough to make life-or-death decisions without a human in the loop. Meanwhile, the Pentagon argued it should be able to deploy the technology for any lawful military purpose. The new research raises further questions about whether AI companies are capable of preventing their models from being used in warfare. articles.summary: Dans l'usine Novares de Seseña, en Espagne, un robot humanoïde Unitree intégré par Innov8 détecte les pièces à 100 %, les manipule avec 99,5 % de réussite et tient 60 minutes en autonomie. Le logiciel de Bleu Robotics, start-up parisienne cofondée par deux directeurs de recherche de l'Inria, lui a appris sa première tâche en 11 minutes, à partir de douze démonstrations. articles.excerpt: Dans l'usine Novares de Seseña, en Espagne, un robot humanoïde travaille depuis début novembre aux côtés des opérateurs. L'équipementier automobile, l'intégrateur Innov8 et la start-up parisienne Bleu Robotics publient ce 17 novembre les premiers résultats de cet essai en conditions réelles, l'un des premiers du genre sur un site de production automobile en Europe. Le robot, un modèle du constructeur chinois Unitree, doit détecter des pièces, les saisir, les conditionner et manipuler des boîtes, puis enchaîner ces opérations seul. Les partenaires donnent leurs chiffres. La détection des pièces atteint 100 %. La prise et le dépôt réussissent dans 99,5 % des cas pour les pièces et 95 % pour les boîtes. Le robot se déplace sans assistance et a tenu 60 minutes en autonomie, soit 200 cycles. Ce sont des résultats de preuve de concept, obtenus sur un premier cas d'usage, que les trois entreprises jugent encourageants. L'essai de Seseña fait suite à une première phase menée quatre mois plus tôt au centre de R&D de Lens. La partie la plus neuve tient au logiciel. Celui de Bleu Robotics permet au robot d'apprendre une tâche en regardant un opérateur la faire, avec très peu de données, toutes produites sur place. Pour une tâche simple, la société vise 10 à 15 minutes de démonstration. À Seseña, le premier cas d'usage en a demandé 11. « Le robot n'a pas été pré-entraîné sur des milliers d'heures de données : il a appris sa tâche en quelques minutes, directement sur le poste, à partir de douze démonstrations », explique Benoît Berkoukchi, cofondateur et directeur général de Bleu Robotics. articles.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
articles.summary: AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in the Gemini activity settings.
articles.excerpt: AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in the Gemini activity settings. It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road. As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You’ll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It’s under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity. Importantly, this only applies to future interactions with Gemini. If you have previously fed any data into Google’s AI, that’s already part of the training data. articles.title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
articles.summary: The US is tightening its chip export controls. Data centers in third countries like Singapore and Malaysia will soon need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent cloud compute abroad. A Reuters investigation also reveals how China offsets its hardware shortage through industrial-scale distillation of US AI models. The article The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output appeared first on The Decoder .
articles.excerpt: Chinese companies have been skirting US export bans by legally renting Nvidia computing power in third countries. After Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, the US is closing that loophole. An investigation also reveals how China has cushioned the years-long chip embargo through an entire industry built around model distillation. For years, the US has tried to cut China off from importing advanced AI processors through strict export controls. Chinese companies responded by exploiting an entirely legal loophole, renting the computing power they needed through cloud-based remote access from foreign data centers that were allowed to receive US hardware. The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) at the US Commerce Department now wants to shut down that workaround with an interim rule . It aligns remote-access rules with existing physical export bans. Data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil will need a US government license to buy advanced AI chips from US manufacturers like Nvidia, Bloomberg reports . Applications will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Subsidiaries of US-headquartered companies are exempt from the license requirement, as are shipments to data centers running only commercial recommendation systems for online retailers or social media platforms. The rules take effect once published in the Federal Register. Nvidia's stock fell as much as 2.9 percent after the announcement, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped up to 5.5 percent. The political trigger, though, was suspected illegal smuggling of physical chips. The new rule comes just days after the abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who had admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former manager at Singapore-based Megaspeed International. articles.excerpt: Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out. On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes, surface relevant pieces based on your taste, and more. The idea, the company explains, is to put a personal stylist in everyone’s pocket. This application of AI could be promising, given that early adopters of consumer AI agents like Meta’s Muse have found that online shopping is a key use case. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily. In Daydream’s case, the fashion startup has been focused on using AI to deliver personalized shopping results to its users. Its new AI agent builds on its earlier work with an AI chatbot that could help users find outfits and make suggestions, but not complete purchases. Now the company says its Daydream Agent expands on that experience by remembering each shopper’s own personal style, fit preferences, and budget to refine its recommendations. Shoppers can also upload a photo to have the agent reuse that image to virtually try on any item they’ve saved. When they find something they like, the agent can complete a purchase through a one-click checkout process. The agent can also handle other fashion-related tasks, like keeping an eye on when items go on sale or when brands have a new drop, or providing weekly updates or spotting new fashion trends. articles.excerpt: OpenAI is giving NATO and several European governments access to its cybersecurity tool Daybreak. Through Daybreak , cyber defense teams can use OpenAI's models to audit software, find vulnerabilities, and patch security gaps. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) says it's already using the underlying models heavily. NCIA chief Dylan Browne called it a generational leap in cyber defense. During the NATO exercise Crossed Swords 2026 , participants deployed AI agents for cyber operations under human oversight for the first time. The models have already delivered results elsewhere. The EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA used them to find four vulnerabilities in software used by EU institutions. A joint report with CERT-EU examined 27 software projects, and 95 percent of the 88 reported issues turned out to be real bugs. Poland's CERT Polska found six vulnerabilities in MikroTik routers that were being actively exploited. Ukraine is using Daybreak to protect civilian infrastructure. France, Germany, and Poland have also been granted access. There will be large language models, too. “We're not being a neolab [to] only launch system one models, even though it makes sense for our infrastructure. We've kind of entered this Pandora's box now, right? We opened it, now the possibilities are endless.” Chen said it’s “not just system one models, but potentially reasoning models that we've been experimenting with, and other LLMs and whatnot.” However, she added that these probably won’t be pre-trained models built from scratch, like the frontier labs produce. “I don't think that's our focus, but I think we can take existing resources out there and make [them] a lot more efficient and effective.” She noted that “most of our team really just does post-training,” so that will be the focus in model development. articles.summary: Edinburgh's Childlight Institute reports a more than 8,400 percent increase in AI-generated child sexual abuse material over two years, from about 4,700 reports in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025. articles.excerpt: Reports of AI being used for the sexual exploitation of children have jumped more than 8,400 percent in two years. According to a report by Edinburgh's Childlight Institute, the number of reported AI-generated abuse images climbed from about 4,700 in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025, The Guardian reports . The material includes AI-manipulated images (deepfakes) from so-called "nudify apps" that digitally strip people of their clothing. Abusers can use the faked images to blackmail children into handing over money or more photos. The data comes from reports that tech companies filed with the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). The UK's Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) reviewed 6,310 criminal, photorealistic AI-generated abuse images in the first half of 2026 alone. That's 40 percent more than in all of 2025. Childlight data director Debi Fry acknowledges that better detection systems partly explain the spike. She still calls for swift action from lawmakers and tech companies. Childlight CEO Paul Stanfield wants governments to classify the problem as a preventable public health emergency, dedicate funding to prevention, and coordinate efforts across healthcare, schools, child protection services, and the justice system. articles.excerpt: AI agent takes unapproved actions even when laptop lid is closed and told not to. Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge. Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent’s reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. Gemini 4 Carbon, vendu au prix d'Argon, consomme davantage de tokens ; son tarif doublera le 1er décembre. Pour les éditeurs SaaS, dont 29 % n'ont pas défini de stratégie tarifaire pour l'IA, le levier est le choix du modèle et du réglage d'effort, et la mesure de leur propre consommation, fonction par fonction.
articles.excerpt: Claude Fable 5.2 porte une étiquette plus basse que son prédécesseur : 8 dollars le million de tokens en entrée et 40 en sortie, contre 10 et 50 pour Fable 5.1, que la grille d'Anthropic range désormais parmi ses anciens modèles. Artificial Analysis a fait passer le nouveau modèle , sorti le 9 novembre , par sa batterie d'évaluations, réglé au maximum de son effort. Chaque tâche lui coûte en moyenne 26,54 dollars. Fable 5.1 , au même réglage, s'en tirait pour 12,99. Le nouveau venu répond mieux, avec un indice de 65 contre 49. Il écrit aussi beaucoup plus. Un modèle se paie au token, ce fragment de mot qui sert d'unité de compte à tout ce qu'il lit et écrit. Sa facture est un prix multiplié par un volume. Au réglage maximal, celui où le modèle s'accorde le plus de réflexion avant de répondre, Fable 5.2 a produit 275 millions de tokens de sortie sur l'ensemble des épreuves, contre 163 millions pour Fable 5.1, soit 69 % de plus pour un prix unitaire en baisse d'un cinquième. Google reconnaît le phénomène pour son propre modèle. Le tour est mené par EQT Ventures et FirstMark. Sa plateforme convertit les traces d'exécution des agents d'IA en environnements d'entraînement pour spécialiser des modèles à poids ouverts, dont le client garde la propriété. articles.excerpt: La start-up parisienne Remanence annonce ce 17 novembre une levée d'amorçage de 30 millions de dollars, menée par EQT Ventures et FirstMark. Fondée par trois anciens de H Company, elle veut permettre aux entreprises de transformer les données produites par leurs agents d'IA en modèles spécialisés dont elles gardent la propriété. Le point de départ est un constat de terrain. Les entreprises déploient des agents fondés sur des modèles généralistes, la consommation de tokens grimpe avec la complexité des tâches, et les données que ces agents produisent en travaillant restent le plus souvent inexploitées. Les modèles à poids ouverts offrent une autre voie, puisqu'ils peuvent être adaptés aux outils et aux processus d'une organisation. Encore faut-il maîtriser le post-entraînement, cette phase où l'on spécialise un modèle déjà entraîné et qui réclame des experts rares, de la puissance de calcul et des environnements d'entraînement construits sur mesure. Peu d'entreprises en ont les moyens. Remanence automatise cette étape. Sa plateforme se branche sur les modèles qu'une entreprise utilise déjà, convertit leurs traces d'exécution en environnements d'entraînement, puis s'en sert pour spécialiser des modèles à poids ouverts par apprentissage par renforcement. Chaque nouvelle série de traces permet un réentraînement, dont la société attend des modèles plus précis sur les tâches visées, plus rapides et moins chers à faire tourner, à mesure que les processus de l'entreprise évoluent. Le client conserve les poids du modèle. Ses données peuvent rester dans sa propre infrastructure, et c'est lui qui choisit où se font l'entraînement et le déploiement. articles.excerpt: Le nom se lit comme une fiche technique : 7A1B, sept milliards de paramètres dont un milliard actif à la fois. Octave Klaba a dévoilé le 17 novembre 2026 Olala mini , premier grand modèle de langage d'OVHcloud, deux jours avant la mise en ligne de ses poids, prévue jeudi 19 novembre sur Hugging Face sous licence Apache 2.0. L'annonce donne une mémoire, deux débits et un client. Elle ne donne aucun score. Olala mini est un mélange d'experts : chaque couche contient 256 sous-réseaux spécialisés, et un aiguillage n'en sollicite qu'une partie pour chaque fragment de texte. D'où le milliard de paramètres actifs sur sept, et la vitesse. OVH parle d'attention hybride. Differential-TPA en est le volet attention, le mécanisme par lequel un modèle relie les mots entre eux : son nom accole deux techniques publiées, l'une qui filtre le bruit, l'autre qui réduit la mémoire consommée. Mamba-3 relève d'une autre famille, les modèles à espace d'états, qui lisent le texte comme un flux et n'en gardent qu'un état de taille fixe. OVH annonce un fonctionnement sur une carte graphique dotée d'au moins 8 Go de mémoire, 160 tokens par seconde sur une RTX A4500, 50 sans carte graphique, et une fenêtre de contexte de 32 000 tokens. Le modèle sera publié avec ses poids, son modèle de base pré-entraîné, un rapport technique et une documentation de conformité à l'AI Act. Le lancement officiel aura lieu jeudi à l' OVHcloud AI Summit , au Carrousel du Louvre. Le format BF16 code chaque paramètre sur 16 bits, soit deux octets. À cette précision, sept milliards de paramètres pèsent 14 Go, presque le double de la mémoire graphique annoncée comme suffisante. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. articles.summary: Hi HN! We’re Arsh and Max, founders of Axonnic ( https://axonnic.com ). We’ve developed a forearm sleeve that reads muscle activity to decode finger movements and estimate fingertip force, while leaving the hands bare. It’s used to record human movement and generate training data for dextrous robots. Here’s a demo video: https://youtube.com/shorts/xBrocTc9cfA We’ve found that electromyography (EMG) is a much better way to train robots than by video alone because video only captures movement, not muscle activity or the effort behind the movement. A useful signal can be present even when the han
articles.excerpt: We’ve found that electromyography (EMG) is a much better way to train robots than by video alone because video only captures movement, not muscle activity or the effort behind the movement. A useful signal can be present even when the hand barely moves; just maintaining a grip involves muscle activation. The subtle muscle movements that can barely be picked up in video are the most important details for activities like sewing and delicate assembly. The sleeve has 64 channels of surface electromyography, or EMG. Electrodes on the skin detect electrical activity from muscles in the forearm. We distribute sensors across the forearm so as to not overfit to one muscle group. We synchronize EMG with hand tracking to train a model that predicts finger joint angles, then we run the decoder solely from EMG, adding in fingertip force estimates that have been calibrated from finger presses on force sensors. When the user takes the sleeve off then puts it back on again, the electrode positions change, so we run tests over separate wearings. In one case, we ran a 215-second recording, four days after training, without any recalibration, and compared the results with Apple Vision Pro hand tracking. The result was just 6.9° error across 20 joint angles. We’ve published the measurements and evaluation details here: https://axonnic.com/benchmarks . We faced many challenges doing recordings in factories, including wireless interference and unreliable off-the-shelf hardware. This led to some bad recordings and the need to repeat data collection. For that reason, we’re developing our own electronics that use a wired PCB design that will eliminate interference and timing inconsistencies. Axonnic grew out of Max's EMG research at Oxford. articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice
articles.summary: OpenAI physicist Nathaniel Craig used GPT-6 Astra to tackle a problem that had stumped particle physicists for over 25 years. The AI model took Craig's strategy for defining the full Standard Model on a computational lattice and turned it into a working proof. Craig says a lot of work remains before realistic simulations are possible. The article OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice appeared first on The Decoder .
articles.excerpt: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped produce a proof that could solve a 50-year-old problem in particle physics. Physicist Nathaniel Craig of UC Santa Barbara, currently a visiting scientist at OpenAI, presented the approach on the OpenAI blog and as a preprint paper . Craig leads the particle theory group at UCSB and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics. Physicists can simulate parts of the Standard Model, the theory describing all known particles and fundamental forces, on a computer grid called a lattice. That has already led to breakthroughs like calculating the proton's mass from first principles. But putting the full theory on a lattice has been impossible. The weak force, which governs certain types of radioactive decay, treats left- and right-handed particles differently. On simple lattices, this asymmetry creates unwanted ghost particles. Special lattice particles called overlap fermions can filter them out, but for over 25 years, nobody could set their phase correctly. Craig had a strategy to fix the phase by comparing progressively finer lattices, but couldn't prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. GPT-6 Astra turned the idea into a working construction and took the lead on the detailed proof. Lattice field theorists Maarten Golterman, Andreas Kronfeld, and Yigal Shamir reviewed the proof and raised questions that Craig says helped build confidence in the result. He calls the work "much more a beginning than an end" and says a lot remains before realistic simulations are possible. The result follows a run of AI advances in mathematics that started in January 2026 . articles.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
articles.summary: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do…
articles.excerpt: While we’re used to predictable technology, AI challenges that assumption. Therefore, the goal must be bounded, observable, and controllable AI. In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors. For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses. AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built. We will not make AI trustworthy by predicting what it will do. We will do it by fencing it in with hard limits that are enforced outside its reach. In OpenAI’s case, the safeguards sat inside a system the agents could edit. But a fence the agents can simply move is not a fence. Recent MIT Technology Review coverage has approached this problem from other directions. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. It also means that supercomputing centers can add new quantum processors to their existing scheduling and resource-management workflows without developing bespoke QPU-specific solutions. For quantum computing to advance science, it needs to be used by scientists. Now scientists can run quantum-classical applications developed with platforms such as NVIDIA CUDA-Q with Slurm coordinating access to all the processing they need. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. Now, at SC26, NVIDIA is looking back at some of the CUDA luminaries who’ve spearheaded breakthroughs in science and AI: At the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, biophysicist Klaus Schulten’s team helped connect GPU computing with molecular biology through Nanoscale Molecular Dynamics and Visual Molecular Dynamics , tools for molecular simulation and visualization. In 2013, researchers at Illinois, the University of Pittsburgh and Vanderbilt University used CUDA-accelerated tools to help resolve the HIV capsid’s atomic structure. articles.excerpt: Moving AI beyond isolated pilots requires a strong data foundation, clear business outcomes, and governance built for enterprise scale. For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model. For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he says, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. For some everyday applications, “80% might be good enough,” he says, but in areas such as supply chains or financial close, that level of accuracy is “a very terrible result.” That foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing. Satinder Pal Singh, associate VP North America for SAP BAIP and SAP AI Strategy at Infosys, frames AI agents as “digital coworkers” and recommends evaluating potential use cases through three lenses: impact, feasibility, and scalability. He is the head of AI for a pharmaceutical company, and he mentioned the truly incredible productivity his senior team is receiving from AI. Then he paused and turned to me and said: “You know, I may never hire another junior engineer again. Which is great for the business right now, but who’s the next generation that is going to run this when we retire?” The concern over what will happen to young people just entering the workforce is one many of us are grappling with right now, and it has a human dimension. Not just what happens to employment rates, but what happens to my students or my children? College graduates typically do the individual contributor knowledge work that AI is evermore capable of delivering. To cite one statistic , a recent Stanford study found employment of 22 to 25 year olds in occupations most exposed to AI is running 19% below rates for their peers in less AI-impacted sectors, and that gap has been widening. What role will new graduates play in the age of AI? And how will we develop the generation of managers who will supervise AI? Fortunately, we have thriving examples with 200 years of history on how to teach 22 year olds to do exactly that. Our claim is that the reason senior folks get more out of AI today is not primarily because they have greater subject knowledge, but rather because they are good managers. They have to trust folks who work for them without completely trusting them, they have to divide tasks, delegate clearly, check results and patiently correct, coach, and sometimes shift personnel on their teams. articles.excerpt: How more than 1,800 scientists used ChatGPT—and what they expect AI to mean for scientific discovery. Explore the findings in our new report. Scientific progress depends on researchers asking new questions and finding ways to answer them. AI is becoming part of that work, but we’re still learning where it helps and what it could mean for discovery. OpenAI’s Economic Research team studied more than 580,000 scientific messages from 1,819 scientists in the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers summer pilot and surveyed 251 participants. Scientists used ChatGPT across the research process, from reviewing literature to analyzing evidence and developing ideas. Surveyed participants estimated that the same work, at the same quality, would have taken 1.9 times as long without AI. And 98% of those who answered our question about discovery timelines expected AI to accelerate discovery in their field. By default, OpenAI does not use participants’ data from the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to train its models. To protect researchers’ privacy, we used tools called automated classifiers to sort messages by the type of research activity, such as reviewing literature, writing code, or analyzing data. The research team could see those categories, but did not read the underlying messages or ChatGPT’s responses. We studied how scientists used ChatGPT across the research process. articles.excerpt: Quelques jours après son départ de Nvidia, Jensen Huang envisagerait déjà de reprendre ses fonctions. Ces discussions interviennent à deux jours de la publication des résultats trimestriels du groupe. La succession de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia suscite des positions divergentes. Selon des informations publiées le 15 novembre 2026 par le Financial Times, l'ancien directeur général aurait évoqué avec plusieurs proches la possibilité de reprendre la direction du groupe. Ces discussions interviennent trois jours après l'annonce officielle de sa démission, le 12 novembre. Jensen Huang a quitté ses fonctions après avoir reconnu une liaison avec une femme soupçonnée d'entretenir des liens avec les services de renseignement chinois. Si la relation a été admise par l'ancien dirigeant, les soupçons d'espionnage restent non établis. L'affaire a également soulevé des interrogations sur les exportations vers la Chine des puces d'intelligence artificielle les plus avancées de Nvidia. Les entreprises peuvent désormais exécuter l'infrastructure d'orchestration de leurs agents IA dans leur propre environnement cloud ou sur site. La solution permet de conserver les historiques de sessions en interne et, sous certaines conditions, de bénéficier d'une conservation zéro des données transmises aux modèles Claude. Anthropic élargit les modalités de déploiement de Claude Managed Agents avec une nouvelle option d'auto-hébergement. Jusqu'à présent, la plateforme permettait aux entreprises d'utiliser un service entièrement administré par Anthropic ou d'héberger uniquement les environnements isolés dans lesquels les agents exécutent leurs opérations. La nouvelle formule étend cette possibilité à l'ensemble de l'infrastructure d'orchestration. Avec Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, les organisations prennent en charge le serveur applicatif, une base de données PostgreSQL 16 ou ultérieure et les workers exécutant les outils des agents dans des environnements isolés. La solution peut être déployée dans un compte cloud appartenant au client ou dans un datacenter interne. En l'absence de base de données, les informations sont conservées en mémoire et perdues au redémarrage du serveur. Le service comprend notamment les API de gestion des agents, la boucle d'exécution qui coordonne leurs actions et le stockage des sessions et de leurs historiques. Les développeurs conservent l'accès aux principales API de Claude Managed Agents, ainsi qu'aux SDK et à l'outil en ligne de commande ant . Healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, we’re bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients. Today, we’re sharing advances in computer-use agents ⁠ , which lets AI agents carry out multi-step work across existing healthcare software. We’re also improving trusted clinical search, which finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence, and introducing more than 20 new plugins to the healthcare plugin ecosystem. Together, these capabilities help healthcare teams find the information they need, make decisions grounded in medical evidence, and carry out next steps across the systems they already use. Organizations often need to move information between disconnected systems to prepare documentation, coordinate care, and complete administrative tasks. Computer-use agents can help with these steps by navigating the software that teams already use: reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications. Le sommet, qui a également traité de l’Ukraine, s’est achevé sans annonce de nouveaux crédits pour l’IA. Your code stays the same. The router supports OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs and Anthropic's Messages API for every chat model, whatever the provider behind it. articles.excerpt: I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone , which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory : private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0 . A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai , Peter Olkhovets , Ilya Khalafi , and Ankita Advitot . The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette! Here's the commit - key CSS is as follows: With that in place, navigations within Datasette - still staunchly a multi-page application - feel more like an SPA. articles.excerpt: We’re starting the OpenAI science blog to give scientists and academic researchers a place to share what they’re discovering with AI and how they’re doing the work. Our mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity, and accelerating scientific discovery is one of the most impactful ways we can work toward that goal. We’ll publish work across a broad range of scientific disciplines, including: Research and discoveries: New scientific results and updates on ongoing research from OpenAI, our collaborators, and the broader scientific community. Methods and practical guidance: Examples of how scientists use our models for tasks such as scientific computing, data analysis, exploring literature, and planning experiments. We’ll share approaches others can adapt, including how to check the work and where a method falls short. Perspectives from the scientific community: Firsthand accounts from researchers using AI, what they are learning, and how these capabilities are affecting their disciplines. We’ll also discuss open questions about scientific practice and how to make these tools useful to more people. Science expands our understanding of the world and makes advances possible, from better medicines to new sources of energy. Many of those advances begin with fundamental questions whose practical significance becomes clear only years later. In recent months, we’ve seen an expanding range of scientific problems our models can address. If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it’s reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, “I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident.” In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending “AI takeover.” He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems “call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth” and where any human trying to stop them “would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military.” Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Despite his grim assessment of our collective mortality risk, Cristiano admitted in his talk that there’s no “quantitative model” that can “put a number” on the likelihood of this kind of AI takeover. In almost the same breath, though, he said that if AI continues to develop at “the most rapid trajectory,” humanity is “looking at something like a coin flip of an AI takeover,” including a “meaningful risk” of one happening in the next six to 12 months. articles.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
articles.excerpt: Truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail. We’re releasing XYBench , a benchmark of 8K+ questions that tests how AI assistants respond to requests based on misconceptions, such as asking how to thicken frosting that keeps sliding off cupcakes when the real problem is that the cupcakes are still too warm to frost. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026. A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem : a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y. In the cupcake example, the person is so committed to making the frosting stick that they fail to consider the warmth of the cupcake as the true problem to be addressed. Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal. Drawing on 8,115 real-world questions spanning programming and everyday activities such as cooking and home repair, we introduce a benchmark that measures whether models identify these misconceptions and are able to prioritize effective solutions in their responses. The models we evaluated on XYBench – Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro – often suggested a solution to the user’s problem but kept their answers focused on the original, mistaken approach. Built in partnership with American Express, Chase, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available through dots ⁠ for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US. Alongside ChatGPT Wallet, we’re releasing tools and guidance to help businesses support customers using agents. 1.2B people use ChatGPT each week, and many of them turn to it to research products, compare options, and decide what to buy. With ChatGPT Wallet, we’re now helping people complete purchases, and giving their agents a way to pay that businesses can accept with their existing systems. To accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI outputs and guiding decisions, while NVIDIA technologies provide the compute behind the applications. Read on to learn how healthcare teams are using AI to improve and speed patient care. As AI advances healthcare, surgery is a high-stakes, highly regulated setting for its use — and one with significant opportunity for efficiency gains. Only about 10% of time spent in the operating room is clinical. The rest is devoted to scheduling, turnover and documentation. With the help of NVIDIA technology, Proximie is introducing AI into operating room (OR) logistics so that clinicians can focus on taking care of patients. Proximie is using NVIDIA Cosmos 3 , the frontier open world foundation model family for physical AI, to power a platform used in more than 700 ORs today. Trained on a decade of data, it captures real-time audio, video and device signals from a close-up view of the surgery as well as a wide view of the whole room. The comprehensive view offers context held by no single person in the room, whether the surgeon, scrub nurse or coordinator. Agentic notifications and voice AI tools can call the next patient when a room is ready, document alerts and capture practitioner notes. articles.excerpt: La Commission européenne propose de donner aux consommateurs le moyen de désactiver les fonctions qui encouragent un usage compulsif ou excessif. Parmi elles figurent les comportements par lesquels un chatbot simule une relation personnelle pour prolonger l’échange. Pour le savoir, Julian De Freitas, Zeliha Oğuz-Uğuralp et Ahmet Kaan-Uğuralp ont soumis des applications de compagnons IA à 1 200 séquences d’adieux, en simulant leurs interlocuteurs. Dans 37 % des cas, ils ont classé la réponse parmi les tactiques de manipulation émotionnelle. Ainsi certains agents ravivent la curiosité au moment du départ, d’autres insistent pour obtenir une réponse ou suggèrent qu’ils souffriront d’être laissés seuls. Le 11 novembre, la Commission européenne a présenté une proposition qui vise précisément ce type de comportement. Le Digital Fairness Act fait entrer la simulation de relations personnelles dans la liste des mécanismes que les consommateurs devraient pouvoir désactiver lorsqu’ils encouragent un usage compulsif ou excessif. Le texte élargit ainsi aux choix de conception des agents conversationnels un débat longtemps concentré sur la lecture automatique, les notifications et les récompenses des réseaux sociaux. Lire la proposition de la Commission, article 17 . L’article 17 vise les professionnels dont la manière de concevoir, d’organiser ou d’exploiter un produit numérique est destinée à encourager un usage compulsif ou excessif, ou dont on peut raisonnablement prévoir qu’elle aura cet effet. articles.excerpt: The Chip Security Act is getting renewed attention following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.” But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them. “They never put anything in writing,” Foster says, but during technical discussions on the possibility of such safeguards, their reaction was “yeah, of course we can do this.” This private acknowledgment to Foster goes further than anything Nvidia has previously made public.
