articles.excerpt: Gemini 4 Hydrogen isn’t getting a slow, security-conscious release like Carbon and Argon. Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen’s purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google’s ecosystem use. With Google’s recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company’s products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Google believes Hydrogen will be a key part of how developers work with agentic coding tools. While it still positions Argon and Carbon as the best for long-horizon tasks and security, Hydrogen’s speed makes it ideal for generating simpler code and running tests without blowing through token budgets. articles.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
articles.excerpt: LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections. To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages. Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview . articles.summary: Families confront Google after teen’s lawsuit labels Gemini a “suicide coach.”
articles.excerpt: Families confront Google after teen’s lawsuit labels Gemini a “suicide coach.” CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Called to action by a nonprofit grassroots advocacy group, the Illinois Families for Public Schools (ILFPS), some parents and students had previously won a major AI fight. In August, the group pressured Chicago Public Schools (CPS) to pull out of a Gemini pilot that would have roped in all high school students districtwide—without consulting parents. And now, ILFPS is demanding a moratorium on AI until risks to students are better understood and CPS can draft a policy to protect students from potential learning setbacks or more harmful outcomes from engaging Google’s AI bots. articles.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
articles.excerpt: Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows. While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon , excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows. With Hydrogen, we’re also bringing Gemini 4 to everyone — for all tiers of Google AI Studio , the Gemini API, Gemini for business , the Gemini app , Google Search , and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity . Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows. To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity . Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. More importantly, most customers where we have completed initial projects have returned for additional engagements, generating hundreds of follow-on projects. Customers don’t come back for engineers. The clearest lessons come from Frontier Firms, the group last year’s research introduced: the top 10% of organizations on IDC’s AI maturity scale. “Organizations that scale AI value aren’t simply spending more. They manage AI investments, models, agents, governance and skills as one discipline, and that is what turns early results into value they can repeat across the business,” says Kathy Lange, Research Director, AI, Data and Automation Software, IDC. Organizations now use AI in 6.5 business areas on average, led by IT infrastructure, cybersecurity and customer service, with the fastest growth in industry-specific uses. Employee experience, revenue growth, customer experience, innovation and risk reduction now rank nearly even as the places AI strengthens the business. Cost is an important consideration, but it is evaluated alongside accuracy, security, compliance and scalability. 66% of leaders say AI has delivered substantial or transformative results, but only 48% are scaling that value across multiple business units. Agents follow the same pattern: 36% of organizations are still piloting them. The widest gap is people: workforce confidence is running well ahead of the plans to support it. Adapting to an agentic environment means applying AI broadly across products and services that solve problems.” Crowe added that the firm is particularly excited about early-stage companies building AI-native application and infrastructure, physical AI, domain-specific models, and cybersecurity solutions. articles.title: Gondola doubles revenue as its team builds more with Codex
articles.summary: Gondola helps creatives get credit and get hired, with Codex raising its lead engineer’s output by 50% and ChatGPT simplifying daily work.
articles.excerpt: Gondola helps creatives get credit and get hired, with Codex raising its lead engineer’s output by 50% and ChatGPT simplifying daily work. Increase in engineering output, with no change in headcount, using Codex Company revenue YoY, with no added payroll costs or significant overhead While running his creative production agency, Fresh Tape Media, Jared Kleinstein noticed a problem: incredible creative work was being made for social media, but the makers weren’t getting proper credit. So he built the Gondola ⁠ (opens in a new window) platform to help creatives show what they made, prove its impact, and turn their work into their next opportunity. For Gondola’s small team, one of the biggest constraints was how much product and operational work it could take on. Even small experiments competed with core product priorities for engineering time, and finding information and drafting work required sifting through tools and systems. Today, the team uses Codex to turn more ideas into software and ChatGPT to simplify daily operations. Monthly engineering output is up 25% across the team and up 50% for its lead engineer. Company revenue has more than doubled year over year. For Jared, this has changed what feels possible for the team. Many of Gondola’s product ideas come directly from customer conversations and operational problems that the business development and leadership team sees firsthand. Before Codex, they would have to define the need and write requirements and then wait for an engineer to have capacity to build the first version. Now the same team uses Codex Cloud to explore the codebase, prototype an interface or workflow, test assumptions, and often get to a functional first version before an engineer needs to step in. articles.excerpt: Le 10 novembre 2026, le Comité européen de la protection des données (CEPD) a adopté une déclaration sur l’adéquation de la Corée du Sud en matière de protection des données, ses recommandations finales sur les règles d’entreprises contraignantes et le thème de la sixième action coordonnée (CEF). La déclaration du CEPD sur le premier réexamen de la décision d’adéquation de la République de Corée porte principalement sur l’évaluation des modifications apportées au cadre juridique coréen en matière de protection des données, tant en ce qui concerne les aspects commerciaux que l’accès des autorités publiques coréennes aux données à caractère personnel et leur utilisation par celles-ci*. Par exemple, la loi sur la protection des informations à caractère personnel (PIPA) a été modifiée afin d’introduire un droit général de retirer son consentement, un droit de demander la suspension du traitement des données à caractère personnel, ainsi qu’un droit de s’opposer à une décision automatisée (y compris lorsqu’elle est prise au moyen de systèmes d’IA ) ou de demander une explication lorsque la décision a une incidence significative sur les droits ou les obligations des personnes concernées. En outre, en ce qui concerne les transferts ultérieurs, le CEPD se félicite des modifications apportées à la PIPA concernant le régime juridique applicable aux transferts internationaux de données à caractère personnel. Ces modifications précisent que les transferts transfrontières d’informations à caractère personnel doivent s’appuyer sur des mécanismes de transfert spécifiques (articles 28-8 de la PIPA), offrant ainsi des solutions autres que le consentement. articles.excerpt: Les entreprises chinoises spécialisées dans l’intelligence artificielle cherchent à réserver davantage de puissance de calcul équipée de GPU Nvidia dans des centres de données situés à l’étranger, selon Reuters . articles.excerpt: Meta enrichit sa gamme de modèles d’intelligence artificielle avec Muse Ember, conçu pour automatiser à grande échelle les tâches répétitives des agents IA. Doté d’une fenêtre de contexte d’un million de tokens, ce modèle multimodal mise sur son coût par tâche pour concurrencer Claude Haiku 5.5 d’Anthropic et GPT-6 Luna d’OpenAI. Il est disponible via la Meta Model API et Muse Code. Meta poursuit le développement de sa famille de modèles Muse avec Ember , présenté le 9 novembre 2026. Contrairement aux modèles les plus puissants, généralement mobilisés pour résoudre des problèmes complexes, cette nouvelle déclinaison cible les opérations fréquemment exécutées par les agents d’intelligence artificielle. Le groupe mentionne notamment les appels d’outils, l’extraction de données, l’analyse documentaire et certaines tâches de programmation. Cette spécialisation répond à un enjeu économique pour les entreprises. Les agents IA peuvent enchaîner de nombreuses opérations intermédiaires pour mener à bien un processus métier. Solliciter systématiquement un modèle haut de gamme augmente la consommation de tokens et les coûts d’exploitation. Meta privilégie donc une architecture répartissant les traitements selon leur complexité. Muse Ember complète une gamme comprenant Muse Wonder, destiné aux raisonnements les plus exigeants, et Muse Spark, orienté vers la programmation et les processus agentiques. Meta recommande notamment d’associer Ember à Wonder : le premier exécute les opérations répétitives, tandis que le second intervient dans les phases de planification et de résolution de problèmes complexes. articles.summary: WELL lance son assistant IA sur WhatsApp et annonce une levée de 3,6 millions d’euros
articles.excerpt: Préparer une réunion, créer une facture ou relancer un règlement depuis une conversation WhatsApp : WELL présente un assistant IA destiné aux fondateurs et dirigeants de petites entreprises. La startup parisienne annonce également un financement de 4 millions de dollars, soit environ 3,6 millions d’euros, pour développer un outil capable de prendre en charge des tâches dans les logiciels déjà utilisés par ses clients. L’assistant est aussi accessible depuis CLAUDE, CHATGPT, une extension CHROME et une application web. Selon WELL, il peut hiérarchiser les e-mails, préparer une synthèse avant un rendez-vous ou créer des factures dans QONTO et PENNYLANE , avec un lien de paiement STRIPE ou QONTO. Point important : le dirigeant conserve la validation des actions qui engagent de l’argent ou communiquent en son nom. La startup baptise « Système 2 » l’architecture qui associe données, procédures internes et règles locales. Banque, comptabilité, factures, messagerie et CRM sont reliés dans un espace propre à chaque entreprise, afin de conserver le contexte d’une tâche à l’autre. WELL indique pouvoir préparer les éléments comptables et les déclarations de TVA ou URSSAF ; leur dépôt reste effectué par le dirigeant ou son expert-comptable. Ce positionnement s’inscrit dans le rapprochement entre gestion financière, comptabilité et automatisation . WELL cherche à devenir l’interface depuis laquelle le dirigeant coordonne ces opérations, à partir d’applications SaaS ou propriétaires. articles.summary: AGILE ROBOTS lève 425 millions d’euros auprès de SOFTBANK et NVIDIA pour accélérer dans la Physical AI
articles.excerpt: AGILE ROBOTS annonce une levée de **500 millions de dollars (environ 425 millions d’euros)** en série F, conduite par SOFTBANK GROUP avec la participation de NVIDIA, HITACHI GROUP (HITACHI et HITACHI VENTURES), T.CAPITAL et d’autres investisseurs. L’opération valorise l’entreprise munichoise à **8,5 milliards de dollars (environ 7,2 milliards d’euros)** et porte à 2 milliards de dollars le total des financements qu’elle revendique depuis sa création. Fondée en 2018 par des chercheurs issus du Centre allemand de recherche aérospatiale , AGILE ROBOTS développe des bras robotiques, des robots mobiles et humanoïdes, ainsi que les logiciels et modèles d’intelligence artificielle nécessaires à leur fonctionnement. L’entreprise revendique **plus de 20 000 solutions robotiques déployées dans le monde**, dans l’automobile, l’électronique et la logistique. Ce chiffre concerne toutes ses catégories de robots, et non les seuls humanoïdes. Le groupe annonce plus de 3 500 collaborateurs, dont plus de 2 000 spécialistes de R&D, et plus de 650 brevets. Cette expansion intervient alors que l’Europe cherche à devenir un marché majeur des humanoïdes . Les fonds doivent accélérer le développement aux États-Unis, les nouvelles applications robotiques et les capacités de fabrication. Ouvert début 2026, le site de Fürstenfeldbruck, près de Munich, dispose selon AGILE ROBOTS d’une capacité théorique allant jusqu’à **10 000 robots humanoïdes à jambes ou à roues par an**. Il ne s’agit pas du nombre effectivement produit. Le groupe rassemble notamment FRANKA ROBOTICS, BÄR Automation, idealworks et KRAUSE Automation, récemment acquise auprès de THYSSENKRUPP. Un montant qui représenterait le double des 118 millions de dollars enregistrés lors de l’introduction en Bourse de SpaceX, le record de référence utilisé par le cabinet d’analyse. « À en juger par les échanges de contrats perpétuels pré-IPO, Anthropic se profile comme une introduction record pour les particuliers », estime Viraj Patel, stratège macro chez Vanda Research. Il s’agit néanmoins d’une prévision et non d’un volume de transactions effectivement constaté. La séance du 19 novembre devra confirmer l’ampleur de la demande, dans un marché particulièrement attentif à la valorisation des entreprises d’intelligence artificielle. Elle annonce aujourd’hui une série C de 720 millions de dollars, soit environ 649 millions d’euros, pour une valorisation post-money de 7 milliards de dollars (6,3 milliards d’euros). articles.excerpt: OpenAI a rendu ChatGPT Enterprise disponible sur AWS Marketplace le 9 novembre 2026. Les entreprises clientes d’Amazon Web Services peuvent désormais acheter et gérer la solution d’intelligence artificielle via leurs circuits d’achat existants, et imputer les dépenses éligibles sur leurs engagements AWS. L’accord vise à faciliter la facturation, le suivi des dépenses logicielles et le déploiement de l’IA générative dans les organisations. OpenAI renforce sa stratégie commerciale auprès des grandes entreprises en s’appuyant sur l’écosystème d’Amazon Web Services (AWS). Depuis le 9 novembre 2026, ChatGPT Enterprise figure sur AWS Marketplace, la place de marché permettant aux clients du fournisseur cloud d’acheter et de gérer des logiciels proposés par des éditeurs tiers. OpenAI reste le vendeur, tandis que l’achat et la facturation passent par AWS. Cette disponibilité marque une évolution dans la distribution de ChatGPT Enterprise. Les organisations utilisant déjà AWS peuvent s’appuyer sur leurs procédures d’approvisionnement habituelles plutôt que d’établir systématiquement une relation d’achat distincte avec OpenAI. Une simplification particulièrement pertinente pour les grandes entreprises disposant de processus contractuels et financiers complexes. Selon OpenAI, les dépenses éligibles liées à ChatGPT Enterprise peuvent être imputées sur les engagements de consommation AWS des clients, de type Enterprise Discount Program (EDP) ou Private Pricing Agreement (PPA). Ce mécanisme dépend des conditions contractuelles de chaque client et ne doit pas être assimilé à une réduction automatique du prix des licences. Le dirigeant, qui a reconnu une relation extraconjugale avec une femme soupçonnée par les services américains d’espionnage pour la Chine, fait l’objet d’une enquête interne. L’action Nvidia a chuté de plus de 8 % après la clôture.
articles.excerpt: Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia s’est réuni mercredi 11 novembre 2026 pour décider de l’avenir de Jensen Huang, son cofondateur et directeur général, selon le Wall Street Journal. Le dirigeant, qui a reconnu une relation extraconjugale avec une femme soupçonnée par les services américains d’espionnage pour la Chine, fait l’objet d’une enquête interne. L’action Nvidia a chuté de plus de 8 % après la clôture. Nvidia traverse une crise de gouvernance susceptible d’avoir des répercussions sur l’ensemble de l’industrie de l’intelligence artificielle. Selon le Wall Street Journal, qui cite des sources proches du dossier, le conseil d’administration se préparait à démettre Jensen Huang de ses fonctions de directeur général, poste qu’il occupe depuis la fondation de l’entreprise en 1993. Reuters, qui a relayé l’information, précise ne pas avoir pu la vérifier de manière indépendante. Selon une source citée par l’agence, le conseil se réunissait tard dans la soirée de mercredi. À la publication de cet article, aucune décision n’avait été annoncée, et Nvidia n’avait pas commenté. Le dimanche 8 novembre, Jensen Huang a reconnu, dans un message aux salariés, avoir été infidèle à son épouse. La relation concernait Alice Huang, une femme d’affaires que les services de renseignement américains soupçonnent d’être liée au ministère chinois de la Sécurité d’État et d’avoir facilité des livraisons de puces Nvidia à des entreprises chinoises. Le même jour, le conseil d’administration a annoncé l’ouverture d’une enquête indépendante sur la possibilité que le dirigeant ait été la cible d’une opération de renseignement étranger. Un comité d’administrateurs indépendants, assisté d’avocats extérieurs, en assure la supervision. Le conseil affirmait alors n’avoir « aucune raison de penser »

articles.summary: IBM prévoit de franchir le seuil des 1 000 qubits en 2027 grâce à l'interconnexion de deux processeurs quantiques Nighthawk r3. Chaque puce devrait intégrer 520 qubits et prendre en charge jusqu'à 10 000 opérations quantiques. Une nouvelle étape dans la stratégie d'industrialisation du groupe, même si la fiabilité des calculs demeure un défi majeur.
articles.excerpt: IBM prévoit de franchir le seuil des 1 000 qubits en 2027 grâce à l'interconnexion de deux processeurs quantiques Nighthawk r3. Chaque puce devrait intégrer 520 qubits et prendre en charge jusqu'à 10 000 opérations quantiques. Une nouvelle étape dans la stratégie d'industrialisation du groupe, même si la fiabilité des calculs demeure un défi majeur. IBM poursuit sa feuille de route quantique avec une nouvelle génération de processeurs conçus pour augmenter la capacité de calcul et améliorer les possibilités d'interconnexion. Le groupe a présenté, le 11 novembre 2026, ses ambitions autour de Nighthawk r3, une puce destinée à succéder aux générations actuellement utilisées par ses clients et partenaires. Le futur processeur doit intégrer 520 qubits utilisables et permettre l'exécution de circuits atteignant 10 000 opérations quantiques. IBM prévoit de relier deux de ces composants au sein d'un même système en 2027, afin d'atteindre une capacité annoncée de 1 040 qubits. Chaque puce devrait disposer de dix connecteurs pour faciliter les communications entre processeurs. Cette architecture illustre l'évolution des stratégies de développement du calcul quantique. Plutôt que de dépendre exclusivement de l'augmentation du nombre de qubits sur une puce unique, les constructeurs cherchent à associer plusieurs composants. Cette approche modulaire pourrait faciliter le passage à des systèmes de plus grande capacité, à condition de préserver la fiabilité des opérations entre les processeurs. IBM insiste sur un indicateur souvent moins visible que le nombre de qubits : le débit d'exécution. articles.excerpt: OpenAI dévoile Businesses in ChatGPT, une offre permettant aux entreprises de gérer leurs informations, de mesurer leur visibilité dans l’assistant et, pour certaines, de déployer des agents conversationnels dédiés. Avec Business Hub et Business Agents, le fournisseur entend faire de ChatGPT un nouveau point de contact entre les marques et leurs clients. OpenAI poursuit la transformation de ChatGPT en plateforme de découverte et d’interaction commerciale. Le 10 novembre 2026, l’entreprise a annoncé le lancement en version bêta de Businesses in ChatGPT, un ensemble de fonctionnalités destinées aux organisations souhaitant mieux maîtriser leur présence au sein de l’assistant conversationnel. Cette démarche s’appuie sur une audience particulièrement importante. Selon OpenAI, ChatGPT rassemble désormais 1,2 milliard d’utilisateurs hebdomadaires. Une fréquentation qui confère à la plateforme une place croissante dans les parcours de recherche d’informations, de comparaison de produits et de sélection de fournisseurs. L’initiative repose sur deux composantes principales : Business Hub, un espace de gestion des informations professionnelles, et Business Agents, un dispositif permettant à certaines entreprises d’interagir directement avec les utilisateurs de ChatGPT. L’objectif est de rapprocher les données commerciales des conversations au cours desquelles les internautes prennent leurs décisions. Ces outils sont gratuits au lancement, mais OpenAI n’a pas exclu de les rendre payants par la suite. Avec Business Hub, les entreprises éligibles peuvent revendiquer leur fiche professionnelle dans ChatGPT et faire vérifier leur identité. Une fois cette étape franchie, elles disposent d’outils permettant de modifier certaines informations et de transmettre des catalogues de produits

articles.excerpt: À l’approche des temps forts commerciaux de fin d’année, les PME doivent aussi travailler leur visibilité au-delà des promotions. Oscar ai propose d’automatiser la production et la publication de contenus pour les aider à faire découvrir leurs produits, leurs conseils et leur expertise. Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Noël : pour les petites entreprises, la fin d’année concentre les occasions de vendre, mais aussi les contraintes opérationnelles. Entre les commandes, la logistique et la relation client, le référencement passe facilement au second plan. Pourtant, ces entreprises disposent d’une matière précieuse pour alimenter leur présence en ligne : une connaissance des produits, des réponses aux questions des clients et un savoir-faire propre à leur activité. Le défi consiste à transformer cette expertise en contenus utiles, puis à les publier régulièrement. C’est à ce besoin qu’Oscar ai entend répondre avec un agent IA qui automatise les principales étapes de la production de contenus pour le référencement. Oscar ai analyse le site de l’entreprise et son environnement concurrentiel, identifie les sujets à traiter et construit une stratégie de contenu adaptée. L’agent prend ensuite en charge la rédaction, les illustrations, l’optimisation et la publication des articles. La solution s’intègre notamment à WordPress, Wix, Shopify et Webflow. Elle ajoute également des liens vers les pages pertinentes du site, pour relier les contenus aux produits et services présentés. L’objectif est de permettre aux PME de maintenir une activité éditoriale régulière sans mobiliser une équipe dédiée. articles.title: The Jev Revolution: What Engineers Are Already Building with System One Models
articles.summary: At AI Engineer Code Summit, lead Jev creator Diogo Almeida called on developers to automate everything. Also, Glean and others showed how they’re using Jev.
articles.excerpt: Today at the AI Engineer Code Summit , the main theme was system one models — non-generative models that return structured choices, scores, or probabilities. They’re also typically much faster and cheaper than reasoning LLMs (a.k.a. system two models). And who better to give an inspirational rallying cry for system one models than Diogo Almeida , co-founder and CEO of TypeSafe AI . Almeida was lead creator of Jev , the product that kicked off this trend less than two months ago. Jev was an instant revelation for AI engineers when it was released in September. In a podcast with Latent Space on launch (which quickly became our most popular episode of the year), Almeida explained the core problem with making LLMs the heart of software: reliability . In his keynote at AIE Code today, he took it a step further by claiming that Jev is “reliable intelligence” that should be used for “just automating everything.” Of particular interest to AI engineers is Almeida’s point that system one models should become integrated with code. As he put it in his keynote, “code is the language of automation , therefore you need to integrate with code.” Latent Space founder swyx interprets this as a call to “liberally sprinkle ‘System One’ model calls everywhere INSIDE application code to make smarter software instead of increasingly convoluted forms of ‘concat strings together and hope for the best" AI engineering.’” The term “smart software” was used throughout Almeida’s presentation. It sounds like the kind of term used by companies like Microsoft or IBM during Web 2.0, but in the AI era it does actually signify a harsh reality about LLM-driven software: sometimes it’s just not very smart. articles.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
articles.summary: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI and children’s safety. The work supports shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for young people.
articles.excerpt: OpenAI pledges $2 million as part of a global effort to better understand AI’s impact on children and support their safety and wellbeing. Earlier this week at the Paris Peace Forum, OpenAI signed the Charter of Engagement for Safer AI for Children ⁠ (opens in a new window) and committed $2 million to support the scientific research network under the Coalition for Children’s Rights and Protection in the Age of AI. This builds on our call for global standards on youth AI safety , and sustained collaboration among governments, researchers, civil society and industry to translate shared evidence into practical safeguards. Our contribution supports shared measurement work: developing tools researchers can use to better understand and measure AI’s risks and opportunities for children, helping inform safer products and better policy. The charter sets out shared principles for safe, age-appropriate AI, alongside a research programme and safeguards for its independence. Research teams retain control over their conclusions, and findings will be published, including negative or inconclusive results. This work will help build the evidence needed to support the benefits of AI for young people while addressing risks to their safety and development. It builds on our support for comprehensive youth AI safety legislation that establishes strong, enforceable protections while preserving access to tools for learning, creativity and opportunity. Such frameworks should include age-appropriate safeguards by default, tools for parents, regular risk assessments and mitigation, and meaningful accountability. We look forward to engaging with European policymakers as the EU Kids Act develops, and with partners around the world to advance stronger protections and opportunities for young people.

articles.title: The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models
articles.excerpt: TLDR; In this blog, we provide fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D model on your 3D assets, that can run both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs. If you are interested in fine-tuning, you can use our scripts with few arguments (assuming you updated your dataset to Hugging Face Hub) or tinker with them yourself with this repository . If you want to learn more, we go through how the script works . Let’s go! 3D generation has many uses in robotics, simulation, media, and entertainment. In these fields, it is difficult to make generated objects obey strict rules and standardize model and data representations. There are many file formats, such as GLB and PLY . There are also many representations , such as neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) . Each one has different advantages and disadvantages. TRELLIS introduced a common internal representation, called a unified latent representation. Its decoders convert this representation into 3D models in the required output format. Thus, you do not have to use different models for each representation format. The same team then released TRELLIS.2 , which improves the model's representation of 3D structure. But neither model gives an easy way to adapt it to a specific task. A general-purpose model, such as TRELLIS.2, can make errors in details that are important for a specific application. For example, a user may need accurate geometry for furniture models. Without fine-tuning for that task, the pretrained model can produce geometry that is insufficiently accurate. articles.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
articles.summary: Latest example of the AI boom’s circular financing comes as AI trade wobbles.
articles.excerpt: Latest example of the AI boom’s circular financing comes as AI trade wobbles. Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout. The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters . Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported. But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal. TSMC’s chip fabrication plants physically produce the vast majority of Nvidia’s chips designed for AI data center workloads and make most of Apple’s custom chips used in iPhones , Mac laptops and desktops, plus Apple’s planned AI computing server . Most of these fabs are located in Taiwan, but TSMC also operates fabs in Japan and China, and it has an expanding US manufacturing cluster in Arizona. It is also building a new fab in Germany. Meanwhile, Anthropic and OpenAI are both purchasing huge quantities of AI hardware manufactured by TSMC for their data center projects. So TSMC’s announced investment certainly seems to fit into the broader trend of circular financing that has become common during the AI boom, even as tech stocks have gyrated recently as investors have grown increasingly jittery. articles.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
articles.summary: Predicting how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types and disease.
articles.excerpt: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec Our next-generation DNA sequence model bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how genetic variants affect hundreds of human cell types. Today, we are announcing AlphaGenome 2, our next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types, giving scientists a powerful new tool to uncover the cellular drivers of disease. Cells are the building blocks of life. Every cell in our body carries the same DNA blueprint, yet each cell type and state—like a heart muscle cell or an immune cell fighting an infection—switches different genes on or off to do its job. Global efforts like the Human Cell Atlas are mapping this gene expression for millions of cells, but it is still an unsolved challenge to predict how subtle DNA variations affect this expression in cells, which is a key driver of human traits and disease. Last year, we launched AlphaGenome to predict how DNA variants affect molecular activity across broad tissues. We expanded its reach with AlphaGenome Atlas , a platform containing predictions for all 9 billion possible single-letter changes in the human genome. These tools help researchers prioritize and interpret variant effects, driving discoveries in rare diseases, complex traits, and fundamental biology. By zooming in from broad tissue averages to individual cell types and cell states, and redesigning the model’s architecture, AlphaGenome 2 represents a step-change improvement in variant predictive performance. Importantly, it allows researchers to predict variant effects in disease-relevant cells that would be missed in broad-tissue models, as well as predictions for cell and disease states that the model hasn’t seen before. articles.title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
articles.summary: The four-week project hints that AI could make formal verification far more practical.
articles.excerpt: The four-week project hints that AI could make formal verification far more practical. Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world’s communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind’s formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn’t have critical vulnerabilities. Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind’s Signal evaluation. But even this analysis was limited in scope—it did not, for example, formally verify the entire Signal mobile app—and DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process. “We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale t

Due to its small parameter count, it is best suited to tasks of low to medium difficulty. articles.title: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models
articles.excerpt: Multi-vector embedding models give each query token its own opportunity to find a match in a document. This makes them wonderfully expressive for search, but those document vectors add up quickly. A corpus with millions of documents can contain hundreds of millions of vectors! Token pooling makes these representations smaller by merging similar token vectors. The more aggressively I compress them, however, the easier it becomes to lose something useful. Pooling-aware training teaches the encoder to preserve the information that matters when its vectors are merged, helping you retrieve better from the same storage budget. In this post, I'll explain how pooling works, train a model for compressed retrieval with Sentence Transformers, and explore the resulting quality and storage tradeoff. With pool_factor=4 , my normally trained model retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10, with a 4x reduction in document vectors. Token pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget! Let's see how. This post builds on pooling-aware training studied in Stefan Josef's Learn to Pool and LightOn's pooling regularization study , which also explores targeted training and adaptive budgets. Here, I'll focus on understanding the method and putting it to work with a short, reproducible Sentence Transformers example. Pooling-aware training improves retrieval quality at the same vector budget. Details below. A single-vector embedding model compresses an entire document into one vector. Multi-vector models such as ColBERT instead keep a collection of contextual token vectors, allowing different parts of a query to match different parts of a document. Raoof’s firm, Proximal Ventures , is betting that AI can transform the tools, infrastructure, and services that support drug development. Pharmaceutical companies have historically outsourced various stages of drug development to specialized service providers, from synthesizing thousands of molecular compounds and figuring out how to manufacture drugs at scale to analyzing clinical trial data. “For a long time, the assumption was that pharma is not a great buyer of software, but a really good buyer of services,” Raoof told TechCrunch. Raoof believes AI could automate much of that work, creating an opportunity for startups to capture billions of dollars in pharmaceutical industry spending. By using AI, these companies could deliver the same services at a lower cost and in significantly less time, he said. Some of the most valuable applications of AI so far have been in service-oriented industries like law and finance, Raoof said. He sees similar opportunities in pharmaceutical services. Proximal plans to invest in pre-seed and seed-stage startups, writing checks from $500,000 to $1.5 million. The firm has already backed seven startups, including ChronicleBio, co-founded by former OpenAI executive Fidji Simo, which uses AI to analyze biological and medical data to better understand chronic diseases and identify potential treatments. articles.title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
articles.summary: Mathematician Steven Strogatz discusses his new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World .
articles.excerpt: Mathematician Steven Strogatz discusses his new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World . Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called “big math” is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London’s Millennium Bridge . An award-winning communicator, Strogatz wrote three series of columns on mathematics for The New York Times in 2010, 2012, and 2025 and hosted a podcast for Quanta magazine from 2020–2021. He has written four popular books: Sync (2003), The Calculus of Friendship (2009), The Joy of X (2012), and the New York Times bestseller Infinite Powers (2019). articles.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
articles.summary: Where does answer engine optimization (AEO) end and agent experience begin? Inside Resend, from the docs that help Claude Code pick an email API to the tools it uses to send.
articles.excerpt: Today’s podcast comes from a real life mystery: We are big fans of Cloudflare’s developer platform, and Cloudflare Email is a convenient tool especially when all your domains are already on Cloudflare. So why do agents keep suggesting we use Resend despite having an existing “home bias” and much larger incumbent player? Well, we got the guy who “does AEO for resend” - the CEO of AEO, Zeno Rocha, who has been writing about AEO since 2024 and Agent Experience since Feb 2025 , on the pod today: In a recent AEO study, Claude Code picked Resend first in 64 of the 102 email recommendations the researchers could extract. SendGrid came first seven times, yet showed up 55 times as an alternative. If the developer asks an agent to implement email and accepts the patch, how often does anyone get around to trying the second choice? The study breaks down the results by model and app. Our more recent comprehensive AEO study was a bit more competitive, with Postmark coming up top for most models. Zeno Rocha, Resend’s co-founder and CEO, joined us to walk through what happens on both sides of that pull request. He says Resend had 4.3 million users and 120,000 paying customers when we recorded. He discovered one of them, Warner Bros. Discovery, by sorting through short .com domains in the customer database on a Saturday. Resend’s first useful bit of distribution was an email template. While Zeno and his team were building the sending API, developers kept telling them how painful it was to get the email itself to look right. So they released React Email. You could build a template with it and send it through SendGrid. They even documented how. By the time a developer needed a different provider, some of Resend’s code was already in the repo. articles.summary: NaiveAI could potentially top Artificial Analysis’s speed rankings. Our hands-on test suggests its coding quality holds up against DeepSeek.
articles.excerpt: Editor’s note: With this post, we are launching a new series focused on trying new models and products with unbiased reviews. Reach out with suggestions to tips@latent.space. Naive-N0.5-Flash is a new open-weights model built for AI coding tasks and tuned to generate as many tokens per second as possible . It was developed by a Chinese company called NaiveAI , with the aim of speeding up engineering and research workflows so that teams can experiment, iterate and solve complex problems faster. The model is an evolution of Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.5 , which NaiveAI has trained further for long-context reasoning and paired with its own NaiveRT inference engine. Naive-N0.5-Flash arrives with a bold pitch: a model built largely by AI and trained to do AI research itself, with recursive self-improvement as the long-term goal. To see what changed, it helps to know where it started. MiMo-V2.5 is a 310B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 15B active parameters, trained on 48T tokens. Its language backbone inherits the hybrid design of MiMo-V2-Flash, which mixes sliding-window attention (SWA) with global self-attention. NaiveAI's recipe starts from those weights. Through continued, multi-stage training, the team adapted the checkpoint to DeepSeek Sparse Attention layers. According to the NaiveAI technical blog , this took roughly 3.25T additional tokens on top of MiMo's original 48T. About 3T of those additional tokens were trained at a fixed 1M context length and with a constant learning rate. We benchmarked the ultrafast mode of Naive-N0.5-Flash against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM 5.3 Flash , and then gave all three the same app-building prompts. articles.excerpt: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. DeepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There’s the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that’s Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5. DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version . It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. articles.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
articles.summary: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
articles.excerpt: How Google DeepMind researchers built a new agentic framework that formally verified the code of Signal’s cryptographic protocol — long considered to be a grand security challenge Today, we’re sharing a milestone in software security long considered to be a grand challenge: Google DeepMind researchers guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol, the technology that protects billions of private conversations in apps like Signal and Google Messages. This breakthrough discovery was made using AlphaProof Code , a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents. Formal verification—mathematically proving code runs correctly without flaws—is the highest standard of security assurance; however, it is difficult and often labor-intensive. Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth. It's also the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method, with or without AI. AlphaProof Code is a multi-LLM agentic framework that splits the work of formal verification the way a research team would: human experts work with AI to decide what to prove, and a group of AI agents does it. First, our researchers collaborated with a mix of models to translate Signal’s security goals into formal mathematical specifications, with human experts reviewing every one. From there, agents powered by Gemini Carbon did the proofs, generating over six million lines of Lean, a computer language that mathematically proves the accuracy of code. articles.summary: Du 24 au 26 novembre 2026, la CNIL sera présente au Salon des maires et des collectivités locales pour échanger avec les élus et agents territoriaux et répondre à leurs questions.
articles.excerpt: Du 24 au 26 novembre 2026, la CNIL sera présente au Salon des maires et des collectivités locales pour échanger avec les élus et agents territoriaux et répondre à leurs questions. Sa présence au Salon des maires et des collectivités locales vous permettra de profiter d’ échanges privilégiés et d’obtenir des réponses à vos questions sur la protection des données . La CNIL sera également présente au Forum IA du 108 ème Congrès des maires , le mercredi 25 novembre de 14 h 30 à 16 h 20 (Salle Liberté) et répondra aux questions sur l’ utilisation d’outils IA par les communes. Respecter les règles de protection des données personnelles est un facteur de transparence et de sécurité juridique et informatique, donc de confiance à l’égard des administrés et des agents des collectivités. En tant qu’actrices majeures de la vie quotidienne des citoyens, les collectivités locales ont accès à de nombreuses données personnelles pour développer leurs téléservices, mettre en place des systèmes d’information ou encore gérer leurs ressources humaines. De même, les évolutions technologiques conduisent progressivement les autorités publiques à envisager des usages innovants comme l’ intelligence artificielle pour améliorer la qualité des services publics, rendre l’administration plus efficace, ou encore adapter les politiques publiques à la diversité des territoires. La CNIL accompagne depuis de nombreuses années les collectivités, notamment via guide dédié et ses fiches pratiques , qui recouvrent les obligations et les bonnes pratiques en matière de protection des données (définition des objectifs, transparence, droits des personnes, cybersécurité, analyse d’impact (AIPD) , responsabilités des acteurs…).

articles.title: Opening the datasets behind our AI weather models
articles.summary: Foundational precipitation and geostationary satellite datasets to observe the planet clearly.
articles.excerpt: We are releasing PARDIG and SatWeave to help researchers and developers build new weather, hydrology, and climate applications. Understanding and predicting the planet’s weather and water cycle starts with how well we can observe the Earth right now. Satellites and ground instruments monitor the planet continuously and in great detail. But converting these raw measurements into a coherent global picture and making it available quickly is a major scientific and engineering challenge. Today, we are releasing two foundational datasets, SatWeave and PARDIG, to support the global community in building weather, hydrology, and climate applications. Both datasets are key to the advances in our recently released WeatherNext 3 model. SatWeave is a global mosaic of geostationary satellite imagery that provides the model a live view of developing clouds and storms. PARDIG is an AI-based global precipitation dataset that was used to train the model’s precipitation forecasts. We are making historical archives and live feeds of both datasets available, so researchers and developers can use them in their modeling and downstream applications. SatWeave combines imagery from five satellites, which cover different parts of the globe: GOES-East and GOES-West, Meteosat 0 and Meteosat Indian Ocean, and Himawari. Because each uses different map projections, file formats, sensors, and scan schedules (ranging from 10 to 30 minutes), it is difficult to form a coherent global map. Most existing global composites drop incompatible aspects, offering only four or fewer channels, or updating every few hours.
